name: T-rex_skull_mm_1-20_scale
description:
## Tyrannosaurus rex Skull

   * Tyrannosaurus rex*
Hell Creek Formation, Montana, USA (~66–68 million years old)

This 3D model is based on the famous MOR 555 “Wankel Rex” specimen, one of the most scientifically important Tyrannosaurus rex fossils ever discovered. The specimen was found in Montana, USA, in 1988 and excavated between 1989–1990 from the Hell Creek Formation.

The skull preserves the deep, powerfully reinforced anatomy characteristic of mature tyrannosaurs. Fused nasal bones, thick serrated teeth, and massive jaw musculature allowed T. rex to generate one of the strongest bite forces among terrestrial animals. Large eye sockets and expanded olfactory regions indicate advanced vision and an exceptional sense of smell.

This specimen is also famous for contributing to groundbreaking studies on microscopic soft-tissue preservation in dinosaur fossils. _(Based on digital data from the Smithsonian Institution 3D Digitization Program. Original scan and digital asset by the Smithsonian Institution.)

name: オウムガイ / Nautilus
description:
生きた化石として有名なオウムガイは、4億年以上もその姿を変えていない。貝の仲間ではなく、イカ・タコなどの頭足綱に属する。貝殻の内部は多くの隔室に仕切られ、100本もの吸盤のない短い腕をもった軟体部が入っている。よく間違えられるが、オウムガイの先祖はアンモナイトではない。アンモナイトはオウムガイから分化した仲間。

Famous as a “living fossil,” the nautilus has remained virtually unchanged for over 400 million years. It is not a mollusk but belongs to the class Cephalopoda, which includes squids and octopuses. The interior of its shell is divided into many chambers, housing a soft body with short arms bearing as many as 100 suckerless tentacles. Although often mistaken, the nautilus is not descended from the ammonite; rather, the ammonite is a group that diverged from the nautilus.

*Amphisbaena alba* is the species from the amphisbaenidae family with the biggest geographic distribution, encompassing all of South America. This species has a diversified diet that includes plants and small invertebrates. The species from the amphisbaenidae family have fossorial habits and spend most of their time burried, wich hinders studies on their ecology. description:
The Orcaelle is a green energy flying vehicle used to transport and large aquatic animal from dangerous places or if they've beached. The flying ship uses a large net function beneath the ship to grab the animal and then lift it into the pool built into the body of the ship. The use of the balloon allows for the ship to easily move the animal back to its habitat.

I used a stylised fill material to make the texture have a handpainted design to the overall look. When it came to devloping my idea, I looked up a list of endangered animals and discovered the Irrawaddy Dolphin, this stemmed the idea of preserving nature and helping animals in general, alongside the use of a renewable way to transport an animal. I based the large blue balloon on the appearance of the Irrawaddy, and placed one in the net of the ship.

Found across the Americas, Africa, and Asia, they inhabit deserts, rainforests, and grasslands. Despite their fearsome look, most tarantulas are docile and pose little threat to humans.

These nocturnal hunters rely on stealth and strength to ambush prey, using their fangs to inject venom and digestive enzymes. They don’t spin webs to catch food but do use silk to line burrows or create egg sacs.

Tarantulas are popular in the exotic pet trade due to their manageable behavior and fascinating biology. With proper care and respect, tarantulas reveal the gentle side of these often-misunderstood arachnids.

name: Equine suspensory apparatus animation
description:
The **equine suspensory apparatus** consists of the interosseus muscle (*M. interosseus medius*), the palmar ligament (*Lig. palmare*) and the proximal sesamoid bones (*Ossa sesamoidea proximalia*) and their sesamoidean ligaments (*Ligg. sesamoidea obliqua and Lig. sesamoideum rectum*).

Disclaimer: The collateral (*Ligg. sesamoidea collateralia*), cruciate and short sesamoidean ligaments (*Ligg. sesamoidea brevia et cruciata*) are not depicted in this animation.

The suspensory apparatus stabilizes the fetlock joint (Articulatio metacarpophalangea) by preventing further overextension during cantering/galloping. It also stores elastic energy during locomotion.

This animation serves as a simplified demonstration of the right equine foot of the forelimb and does not claim complete scientific accuracy of the equine foot anatomy.

Animation and sculpting of model done in Blender. 3D scanning of bones performed with the structured light scanners “Artec Leo’” and “Artec Space Spider”.
